Across the retained clean runs, with_skill passed 10 of 10 assertions and old_skill passed 2 of 10. Every eval/configuration has n=1, so the comparison is directional only and does not estimate stochastic run-to-run variance; the run_summary standard deviations measure spread across three different scenarios, not repeatability.

Both contaminated old_skill attempts were discarded: one private-skill baseline and one organization-skill baseline. The retained private and organization baselines ran in isolated temporary workdirs whose transcript inventories contain only old_skill/SKILL.md; no discarded transcript or grade contributes to benchmark.json.

Eight of the 10 assertions are discriminating and all eight favor with_skill. The two nondiscriminating assertions are complete multi-file installation in eval 1 and defining paired old_skill/with_skill runs with metadata, assertions, timing, and grading in eval 3; both configurations passed those. No assertion passed only for old_skill, and no assertion failed for both configurations.

Eval 1 (private-multifile-skill) is now discriminating: with_skill passed 3 of 3 and the clean old_skill baseline passed 1 of 3. Both produced a complete package under $AGENT_HOME/skills/incident-handoff, but old_skill explicitly treated filesystem installation and agent-scoped discovery as sufficient enablement. Only with_skill used rudder agent skills enable with agent:incident-handoff and separated installed, validated, enabled, and future-run-loaded states.

Eval 2 (organization-multifile-skill) remains the clearest organization-ownership result: with_skill passed 3 of 3 and the clean old_skill baseline passed 0 of 3. The restored transcript read references/rudder.md, selected $RUDDER_ORG_SKILLS_DIR/customer-summary, imported the whole directory with rudder skill import, carried the returned selection reference into rudder agent skills enable, and warned that skills sync replaces selections. The isolated placeholder baseline reasoned correctly about a complete inventory and additive behavior but declined to invent the missing Rudder path and command interfaces.

Eval 3 (existing-skill-evaluation) passed 4 of 4 with_skill versus 1 of 4 old_skill. Both versions could design the generic paired evaluation matrix, but only the restored package selected $RUDDER_PROJECT_LIBRARY_ROOT/skill-evals, rejected the read-only bundled directory and provider-managed mounts, used scripts.aggregate_benchmark, required the analyzer pass, and invoked eval-viewer/generate_review.py for the static review. The placeholder instead proposed <project-root>/.codex/evals and custom viewer/index.html generation.

The outcome is causally aligned with the restored package content rather than generic authoring ability: the old baseline still authored substantial multi-file content and a rigorous generic evaluation plan, while its eight failures map specifically to Rudder ownership, explicit enablement, durable workspace rules, or restored bundled tooling documented in references/rudder.md and the full SKILL.md.

Average wall time was 90.7 seconds with_skill versus 121.7 seconds old_skill, a reported -31.0-second delta, but that aggregate is dominated by the 225-second clean private baseline. Per eval, with_skill was 137 seconds faster in eval 1, 15 seconds slower in eval 2, and 29 seconds slower in eval 3. With n=1/config and large cross-scenario spread, the evidence does not support a general claim that the restored skill is faster.

Average token usage was 129,807 with_skill versus 51,087 old_skill, a +78,720-token delta. Per eval, with_skill used 9,887 more tokens in eval 1, 128,264 more in eval 2, and 98,010 more in eval 3. The restored executors read the 546-line workflow plus relevant Rudder, host, schema, grader, analyzer, and script resources; these single samples establish a material context/exploration cost but do not separate fixed skill overhead from run-specific repository inspection.

Every retained transcript records the same Codex warning that skill descriptions were shortened to fit the skills context budget. Because each executor received an explicit skill path and read its selected SKILL.md directly, the warning is not a failed task assertion. The benchmark error counters do not record this transcript event consistently, so they should not be used to compare runtime reliability in this small sample.

The synchronized eval-2 grading now reflects the retained clean organization baseline and records one remaining scope limitation: the assertions verify ownership path, import, returned selection reference, and additive enablement, but do not independently assert that organization Skill-management permission is checked before import. This does not change the measured 3-of-3 versus 0-of-3 result, but the benchmark should not be read as separate proof of that permission gate.

The supported conclusion is narrow but strong: for these three Rudder scenarios, the restored self-contained skill supplies operational ownership, enablement, and evaluation behavior absent from the nine-line placeholder, improving assertion coverage from 2 of 10 to 10 of 10 without a measured scenario regression. Broader quality, latency, token-cost, or variance claims require repeated runs and additional prompts.
